Done. The implementation is complete in `paasio.go`, and all tests pass with `go test -race` (plus clean `go vet` and `gofmt`).

What I did:

- **`readCounter`** — wraps an `io.Reader`; `Read` delegates to the underlying reader, then updates the byte total (`n`) and operation count (`ops`) under a mutex. `ReadCount` returns both values while holding the same lock.
- **`writeCounter`** — the mirror image for `io.Writer`, with `Write`/`WriteCount`.
- **`readWriteCounter`** — embeds both `readCounter` and `writeCounter`, each pointing at the same `io.ReadWriter`, so it satisfies `ReadWriteCounter`.

Two details worth noting:

1. The `ReadCounter`/`WriteCounter`/`ReadWriteCounter` interfaces were already declared in the existing `interface.go`, so `paasio.go` only defines the concrete types and constructors.
2. The byte and op counters are updated and read together under one mutex. This is what the consistency tests (`testReadCountConsistency`, `testWriteCountConsistency`) require — `ReadCount`/`WriteCount` must always observe `nops == n / bytesPerOp`, which is only guaranteed if both counters change atomically.
